messages.subject: indicator functions
parts:
Hello,

Anyone knows whether it is possible to define indicator functions within a model specification constraint? e.g. y==(f>0)*1 would this expression give me  y=1 when f>0 and y=0 when f<0?

Many thanks,
Susana

messages.author: 4da793840121242b
messages.subject: Re: indicator functions
parts:
'y' represent a vector of observations and 'f' a factor. Below is the full model specification.

model1 <- '#
y1 ~  NA*x
y2 ~ NA*f2
f2 =~ NA*x
#variances and covariances
y1~~f2
y1~~y1
y2~~y2
f2~~1*f2
# intercept
y1 ~ 1
f2 ~ 1
# constrains
y2==(f2>0)
'

Thanks,
Susana

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: indicator functions
parts:
To my knowledge, the factor scores are not estimated during the maximum likelihood estimation. Rather, the model-implied covariance matrix is computed to be as close as possible to the sample covariance matrix. Therefore, the constraints defined from factor scores are not possible. I may be wrong though.

I may use Bayesian-estimation programs (e.g., winbugs, openbugs, stan, or jags) to estimate this model. In Bayesian framework, factor scores of each individual can be treated as parameters so the selection variable might be possible.

Sunthud
